q: How many days are in a leap year?
x: An extra day, February 29, is added about every four years because Earth takes roughly 365.25 days to orbit the Sun.

q: Who is credited with patenting the telephone in 1876?
x: Bell reportedly said the first words over a telephone to his assistant: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.'

q: Which holiday is known for carved jack-o'-lanterns?
x: The custom began in Ireland and Scotland, where people carved turnips; pumpkins became popular in North America.

q: What does the 'www' in a web address stand for?
x: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at the CERN research center.

q: Which company makes the iPhone?
x: Apple unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007, combining a phone, an iPod, and an internet device.

q: What is the official currency of the United Kingdom?
x: The pound is one of the oldest currencies still in use, with roots going back over a thousand years.

q: Which artist painted the Mona Lisa?
x: Leonardo worked on the portrait for years and kept it with him until he died in France in 1519.

q: Which flower is traditionally given on Valentine's Day?
x: Red roses have symbolized love for centuries, and millions are sold around February 14 each year.

q: What does ATM stand for?
x: The first modern cash machine was installed in London in 1967.

q: Who co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen?
x: Gates and Allen founded Microsoft in 1975 to write software for early personal computers.

q: What is a scientist who studies stars and planets called?
x: The word comes from Greek roots meaning 'star law'.

q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
x: Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission.

q: A word that means the same as another word is called what?
x: Synonym comes from Greek words meaning 'same name'. A thesaurus is a book full of them.

q: What do you call a word made from the first letters of a phrase, like NASA?
x: Acronyms are pronounced as words, while initialisms like FBI are spoken letter by letter.

q: Which of these words reads the same forward and backward?
x: Words like this are called palindromes, from Greek words meaning 'running back again'.

q: How many sides does a standard stop sign have?
x: The octagon shape lets drivers recognize a stop sign from behind, even if the face is covered in snow.

q: Which computer key deletes the character to the left of the cursor?
x: The name comes from typewriters, where the carriage moved back one space.

q: What does GPS stand for?
x: GPS was built by the US military, and its satellites broadcast time signals that your phone uses to work out where you are.

q: What does the 'PIN' in PIN code stand for?
x: Most bank card PINs are four digits long, which allows 10,000 possible combinations.

q: Which holiday is celebrated on July 4 in the United States?
x: It marks the 1776 adoption of the Declaration of Independence and is famous for fireworks.

q: Which month of the year has the fewest days?
x: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year, a quirk inherited from the ancient Roman calendar.

q: On which US holiday do families traditionally serve roast turkey?
x: Turkeys are so central that the US president 'pardons' one every year before the holiday.

q: Which vitamin does your skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
x: Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium for strong bones.

q: About how many hours of sleep do most adults need each night?
x: Health experts say regular sleep in this range supports memory, mood, and the immune system.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the human body?
x: An average adult heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day.

q: How many teeth does a typical adult have, including wisdom teeth?
x: Children have 20 baby teeth, which are gradually replaced by permanent ones.

q: Which famous iron tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris?
x: It was meant to stand for only 20 years, but its use as a radio antenna saved it from demolition.

q: Which white marble monument in Agra, India, was built as a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal?
x: Emperor Shah Jahan ordered it built for his beloved wife; construction took about 20 years.

q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
x: The statue arrived in 350 pieces packed in more than 200 crates and was dedicated in 1886.

q: What is the extra money a bank pays you for keeping savings in an account?
x: Interest that earns more interest is called compound interest, and over decades it can multiply savings.

q: What is the word for money that one person owes to another?
x: The word comes from the Latin 'debitum', meaning 'something owed'.

q: A business's income minus its costs is called what?
x: When costs are higher than income, the result is a loss instead.

q: Which currency is used by Germany, France, and Spain?
x: Euro banknotes and coins entered circulation in January 2002.

q: Which inventor is most famously linked with the practical light bulb?
x: Edison's team tested thousands of materials for the filament before finding one that lasted.

q: Which brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903?
x: The first flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, lasted only 12 seconds.

q: Which German inventor introduced movable-type printing to Europe in the 1400s?
x: His printing press made books cheaper and helped spread literacy across Europe.

q: What does USB stand for?
x: USB was introduced in the mid-1990s to replace a confusing mix of ports on computers.

q: What does CPU stand for?
x: The CPU is often called the brain of a computer because it carries out program instructions.

q: What does PDF stand for?
x: Adobe created the format in the early 1990s so documents would look the same on any device.

q: Which company develops the Android operating system?
x: Google bought Android Inc. in 2005, and the first Android phone appeared in 2008.

q: In which language is 'bonjour' a common greeting?
x: It literally combines 'bon' (good) and 'jour' (day).

q: What does the Spanish word 'hola' mean in English?
x: Unlike many Spanish words, 'hola' starts with a silent 'h'.

q: What does the German word 'danke' mean?
x: It is related to the English word 'thank'.

q: How many letters are in the modern English alphabet?
x: The letters J, U, and W were the last to be added to the Latin alphabet used in English.

q: What do you call a book that lists words and their meanings?
x: Noah Webster published his famous American dictionary in 1828.

q: What do you call a book of maps?
x: The name honors the Greek Titan Atlas, whose picture appeared on early map collections.

q: Which reading system for blind people uses raised dots?
x: It was invented by a Frenchman, Louis Braille, who was blind himself.

q: Which signaling code is made of short dots and long dashes?
x: Samuel Morse helped develop it in the 1830s and 1840s for the electric telegraph.

q: Which physicist developed the theory of relativity?
x: Einstein published his special theory of relativity in 1905, a year often called his 'miracle year'.

q: Which nurse became known as 'the lady with the lamp'?
x: She improved hygiene in military hospitals and is considered the founder of modern nursing.

q: Which Dutch artist painted 'The Starry Night'?
x: Van Gogh painted it in 1889 while staying at an asylum in Saint-Remy, France.

q: Which Scottish scientist discovered penicillin in 1928?
x: Fleming noticed that mold on a forgotten dish had killed the bacteria growing around it.

q: Which Apple co-founder introduced the first iPhone in 2007?
x: Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976, left in 1985, and returned in 1997 to lead its comeback.

q: Who founded Amazon in 1994?
x: Bezos started the company in his garage in Washington state, initially selling books online.

q: Which brand uses the slogan 'Just Do It'?
x: The slogan debuted in 1988 and is one of the most recognized taglines in advertising.

q: Which company is famous for its golden arches logo?
x: The arches were part of the architecture of early restaurants before becoming the logo.

q: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
x: It contains hundreds of billions of stars and is shaped like a giant spiral.

q: Which star is closest to Earth?
x: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach us; the next closest star is over four light-years away.

q: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
x: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

q: Which planet is nicknamed the Red Planet?
x: Iron oxide, or rust, in its soil gives Mars its reddish color.

q: How many planets orbit the Sun in our solar system?
x: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

q: On which holiday do many people make resolutions for the coming year?
x: The tradition of making fresh-start promises goes back to ancient Babylon.

q: Valentine's Day falls on which date?
x: The day is named for a saint named Valentine, and the date has been linked to romance since the Middle Ages.

q: How many animals appear in the Chinese zodiac?
x: Each animal represents one year in a repeating 12-year cycle.

q: Which major festival of lights is celebrated across India each autumn?
x: Homes are decorated with oil lamps and lights to symbolize the triumph of light over darkness.

q: How many bones does a typical adult human body have?
x: Babies are born with around 300 bones, and many fuse together as they grow.

q: For about how many seconds should you wash your hands with soap?
x: Scrubbing for at least 20 seconds helps lift germs off your skin, about the time it takes to sing 'Happy Birthday' twice.

q: Which mineral found in milk helps build strong bones and teeth?
x: About 99 percent of the calcium in your body is stored in your bones and teeth.

q: Normal human body temperature is about 98.6 degrees on which scale?
x: That equals about 37 degrees Celsius, though the true average varies from person to person.

q: What does the first aid term CPR stand for?
x: CPR uses chest compressions to keep blood moving to the brain until medical help arrives.

q: What is the name of the US coin worth one cent?
x: The Lincoln penny, introduced in 1909, was the first US coin to feature a real person.

q: How many cents is a US dime worth?
x: The dime is the smallest in size of all current US coins even though it is worth more than a penny or nickel.

q: What plastic card lets you borrow money up to a set limit and pay it back later?
x: Unlike a debit card, a credit card spends the bank's money first, and interest applies if you do not repay in time.

q: What do we call a company's recognizable name, logo, and reputation?
x: The word comes from the practice of burning a mark onto livestock to show ownership.

q: What is a share of ownership in a company called?
x: Owning stock makes you a part-owner, and its price rises or falls with the company's fortunes.

q: In which art form do dancers wear pointe shoes?
x: Ballet began in the Italian Renaissance courts and was developed further in France.

q: What is the Japanese art of paper folding called?
x: The word means 'folding paper', and a traditional crane is the best-known design.

q: What is the traditional Japanese robe with wide sleeves called?
x: Kimono literally means 'thing to wear'.

q: What is the traditional pleated Scottish garment worn around the waist by men called?
x: Each clan traditionally has its own tartan pattern.

q: Which famous ancient monuments stand near Cairo, Egypt?
x: The Great Pyramid was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for about 3,800 years.

q: Which clock tower stands beside the Houses of Parliament in London?
x: Strictly, Big Ben is the name of the great bell inside the tower, not the tower itself.

q: Which mountain memorial in South Dakota features four carved US presidents?
x: Carving took 14 years, from 1927 to 1941, and about 400 workers took part.

q: What is a small digital picture used to express a feeling in messages called?
x: The word comes from Japanese and means 'picture character'. It has nothing to do with the English word 'emotion'.

q: What is the name of Apple's voice assistant?
x: Siri first appeared on the iPhone 4S in 2011.

q: Which company owns the video platform YouTube?
x: Google bought YouTube in 2006, just 18 months after it was founded.

q: What does 'AI' stand for in technology?
x: The term was coined by computer scientist John McCarthy for a 1956 workshop at Dartmouth.

q: In most programs, which keyboard shortcut copies selected text?
x: The 'C' is easy to remember for 'copy', and Ctrl+V pastes it.

q: On a standard traffic light, which color means stop?
x: Red was chosen because it is visible from far away.

q: Which alphabet is used to write Russian?
x: It is named after Saint Cyril, a missionary to the Slavs in the ninth century.

q: What do you call a doctor who specializes in treating children?
x: The word comes from Greek roots meaning 'child healer'.

q: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
x: Daniel Fahrenheit built the first reliable mercury thermometer in 1714.

q: How many bits are in one standard byte?
x: A single byte can represent 256 different values, enough for one text character in early computers.

q: Which phone number do you dial for emergencies in the United States?
x: 911 was first used in 1968 and now connects callers to police, fire, and medical help.

q: Which color is most associated with St. Patrick's Day?
x: Cities such as Chicago dye their river green each year for the celebration.

q: On which holiday do children traditionally hunt for decorated eggs?
x: Eggs became a symbol of new life in spring long before they were dyed and hidden.

q: In which month is Mother's Day celebrated in the United States?
x: It is held on the second Sunday of the month and became an official US holiday in 1914.

q: What does CEO stand for?
x: The CEO is the highest-ranking manager in a company and reports to its board of directors.

q: What do we call the money people and companies pay to the government from income and purchases?
x: Benjamin Franklin wrote that nothing is certain but death and taxes.

q: Which tool uses a magnetic needle to show direction?
x: Early compasses were made in China more than 2,000 years ago.

q: How many cards are in a standard deck of playing cards, not counting jokers?
x: The four suits each have 13 cards, and the 52 cards roughly match the number of weeks in a year.
